soundness_flags.label: thm:whole-set-coverage
soundness_flags.one_line: Given P∈Γn with Bonferroni probability at least 1−η, Θv(P)⊆⋃P′∈ΓnΘv(P′) follows immediately by the definition of the union estimator, so this root theorem is a routine set-inversion corollary with no independent kernel.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2104.04590v4, April 2026 preprint corresponding to the cited forthcoming article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper converts a known rational conditional likelihood into conditional moment equalities and PSD moment-space restrictions; Assumption 2.1 treats the latent effect distribution conditional on observed W and requires a specified likelihood kernel.
The cited paper gives existence characterizations for truncated Stieltjes sequences supported on [0,∞), including PSD and range conditions in the even case.
The paper constructs identified-set estimators and confidence regions by inversion of a sample criterion and studies consistency, rates, and inference.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Demote thm:whole-set-coverage to a corollary, or replace it with a substantive result on computable inversion, diameter contraction, or a boundary-valid refinement beyond the tautological Clopper–Pearson union.

Make the strict-cone contribution operational by adding a certified atom-extraction construction with an explicit finite support bound and a worked non-grid numerical instance comparing weak and strict fibers.
Promote the c→1 question into a sharper theorem target by naming a particular adjacent-rank stratum and an explicit least-favorable sequence or directional limit functional.

recommended_next_step: Revise the routine whole-set-coverage root theorem into a corollary or substantive inference target, then advance the exact response-type/Stieltjes cone as the field-tier kernel.
